utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Good morning, everybody. I have to inform the parties that Judge Fassi Fihri unfortunately is ill in hospital today and, therefore, unable to attend this hearing. The remaining Judges conferred under Rule 15 bis and came to the conclusion that it's in the interest of justice to continue sitting in this part-heard case for a period of not more than three days. Are there any observations to this by the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have any objections, Your Honour. We are ready to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Nor do we, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. In the light of this, I think we have to take into account to use -- make use of these three days in the best possible way. And from my point of view, that means that we can hear the witnesses from abroad today and, worst-case thinking, in case - and we don't hope that it will be the case - Judge Fassi Fihri is not available for next week, that the witnesses coming from abroad can be heard next week. So therefore, if we could know what is envisaged now actually for next week, what are the upcoming witnesses from abroad?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, next week, we actually did not have a witness for Monday, other than -- there still are two reports outstanding. We are hoping to simply submit those reports if they are accepted by the Court and the Defence. One of them should be ready today. However, it uses the 65 ter numbers, and we are going to give it to the Court and the Defence today, but we may try to put in the S numbers and give you a supplemental version of that later. That's the document analysis or the linguistic report. The demographic report, I was promised Monday at the latest. We're checking on where that is. But we do have a witness from abroad on Tuesday, and we think it's a two-day witness. It's Witness Number 33.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore, we discussed it beforehand. We think it's appropriate to hear today the witness, and then continue next Tuesday with the next witness for the remaining two days under Rule 15 bis. And in the light of this, we should avoid anything unnecessary to deal with today. And therefore my question goes to the Office of the Prosecutor: When will the witness of today be available in order that we can proceed and start with the hearing of this witness immediately, and then conclude this witness today, even though it might be later than 4.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I know Ms. Sutherland was meeting with the witness just this morning, so we anticipated 11.00. She will be available and ready to testify. If we could try to contact her, I doubt we could move it up much. It's possible we could move it a very little. And there are several statements we discovered recently to go over with her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And those statements, can they be distributed or are they already distributed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. So then I think it's advisable also in the light that we have to take care of the interests of the interpreters, that we start immediately when we have the green light of the OTP with the witness. And I think we should all stay tuned and start then when we have heard that we can begin with this witness and don't do anything else. And please, our apologies to Mr. Sebire that we, for reasons he will hopefully understand, don't want to hear him today, that we really concentrate on the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, two things, then: Of course, we understand the problems. Mr. Sebire was due to go on a fact-finding mission to do with the other case on Sunday. If Your Honours would want to hear him next week, do I understand? I'm not saying it couldn't be prevented. It can be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We shouldn't try to schedule anything else for next week than to hear the witness from abroad. As I mentioned beforehand, in case Judge Fassi Fihri wouldn't be available.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Then, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we can combine this, as you may know, there were some remaining questions from the cross-examination by the Defence, and then it can be combined with the questions by the Judges, and at the same time with the hopefully upcoming new table on the witnesses mentioned in the annex to the fourth amended indictment. And this can be done probably the week after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. May I say, the other witness that was intended to call next week was Mr. Brown. But from what you're saying, Your Honours, it may not be possible to call him either next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Simply this, it's for my benefit, I was hoping to address all Your Honours this morning on a question of some of the matters you raised on Monday. I don't know whether Your Honours would consider it appropriate in the absence of Judge Fassi Fihri or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it would be better, and assist the Chamber if we could do it in the presence of Judge Fassi Fihri, and that we indeed continue this way, that we adjourn now and stay tuned. And please let us know immediately when the witness is ready for hearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May I just ask one thing, and this does have an effect. Your Honours, when I heard the transcript, indeed I was watching what Your Honour said about the witnesses the Chamber intended to call, there was a mention of the bishop of Banja Luka, but I hadn't worked out at the end whether Your Honours were intending to call him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No. Quite clear. Not at this time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Times may change. We mentioned the name in the hearing yesterday, and the parties will receive the invitation letter filed in due course.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned we know from the OTP that the witness is ready for being heard. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we could say 11.00 unless notified sooner because definitely we'll be ready at 11.00 but we'll notify you if she's available sooner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this. --- Break taken at 9.49 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. We are in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness Number 16, we had requested or -- I don't think we formally requested, we are requesting a pseudonym for that witness. It's a 92 bis witness. That's the only protective measure. Obviously the Defence has the name. Mr. Lukic, is there an objection to Witness Number 16 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could we please refrain from discussing any additional matters save hearing the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can we go to closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Can we please go to closed session.
